title: From LLM-Generated Specifications to Learned Quadruped Locomotion
abstract: arXiv:2609.07111v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Quadruped robot locomotion policies are often trained using reinforcement learning, which in turn relies heavily on hand-crafted reward functions. Designing reward functions requires substantial manual engineering, and it is often unclear which local rewards will induce the desired global behavior. Shaped rewards from formal specifications in languages like Signal Temporal Logic (STL) can make rewards more interpretable, but writing STL specifications itself still requires domain expertise. We study whether large language models (LLMs) can fill this gap by generating Parametric Signal Temporal Logic (PSTL) specifications that are subsequently used for policy learning. Given a natural language locomotion objective and a constrained specification grammar, GPT-5.5 and Qwen 3.6 independently propose STL templates for command tracking, safety, and gait structure. translated_title: 从大语言模型生成的形式规约到学习的四足机器人运动
translated_abstract: 四足机器人的运动控制策略通常使用强化学习进行训练，而这又在很大程度上依赖于手工设计的奖励函数。设计奖励函数需要大量的人工工程工作，而且往往不清楚哪些局部奖励会诱导出期望的全局行为。利用信号时序逻辑（STL）等语言的形式化规约进行奖励塑形可以使奖励更具可解释性，但编写STL规约本身仍然需要领域专业知识。我们研究大语言模型（LLM）能否填补这一空白，即由大语言模型生成参数化信号时序逻辑（PSTL）规约，并将其用于后续的策略学习。给定一个自然语言描述的运动目标和一个受约束的规约语法，GPT-5.5和Qwen 3.6独立地提出了用于命令跟踪、安全性和步态结构的STL模板。我们使用专家数据来实例化所生成的PSTL模板的参数……
tldr: 本文提出利用大语言模型根据自然语言运动目标自动生成参数化信号时序逻辑（PSTL）规约，以替代人工设计奖励函数，实现更可解释且省力的四足机器人运动策略训练。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes using large language models to automatically generate Parametric Signal Temporal Logic (PSTL) specifications from natural language locomotion objectives, replacing hand-crafted reward functions for more interpretable and less labor-intensive quadruped robot locomotion policy training.
